# freshdesk_email_mailbox (Resource)

A support mailbox that turns inbound email into tickets.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the mailbox.
- `support_email` (String) Address customers write to.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the mailbox is accepting mail.
- `custom_mailbox` (String, Sensitive) IMAP and SMTP settings as a JSON object with `incoming` and `outgoing` keys, each taking `mail_server`, `port`, `user_name`, `password`, `use_ssl` and `delete_from_server`. Only used when `mailbox_type` is `custom_mailbox`.

~> Freshdesk never returns the password, so this attribute is not refreshed from the API and drift in it cannot be detected.
- `default_reply_email` (Boolean) Whether outgoing replies are sent from this address.
- `disable_verify` (Boolean) Whether to skip ownership verification when creating.
- `group_id` (Number) ID of the group tickets from this mailbox are assigned to.
- `mailbox_type` (String) `freshdesk_mailbox` for a Freshdesk-hosted forwarding address, or `custom_mailbox` for one you own and reach over IMAP.
- `product_id` (Number) ID of the product this mailbox belongs to.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the mailbox was created (RFC 3339).
- `forward_email` (String) Address to forward mail to, for a Freshdesk-hosted mailbox.
- `id` (String) Numeric identifier of the mailbox.
- `updated_at` (String) When the mailbox was last changed (RFC 3339).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by numeric ID.
terraform import freshdesk_email_mailbox.example 42
```
